$comment: The application version is the product version and drives the v* tags that
the packaging workflow releases from. The MIT libraries under packages/*
are not versioned independently yet. They are not published to npm, and
adding per-package releases before anyone depends on them would be
ceremony without a consumer. Add them here when the first one publishes.
$versioningComment: Stay in 0.x until 1.0 is a deliberate decision rather than a side effect of
the first feat: commit. While below 1.0, a feature bumps the minor and a
breaking change bumps the minor too. Nothing here is stable enough yet for
$initialVersionComment: Without this, release-please reads the 0.0.0 manifest entry as 'never

$componentComment: package-name is deliberately empty. release-please compares the component
parsed from the release branch name against getBranchComponent(), which is
`this.component || getDefaultComponent()`. That helper does NOT consult
include-component-in-tag, so any non-empty name makes it expect a component
the grouped branch (release-please--branches--main) does not carry, and the
release is silently skipped with a warning while the workflow still reports
success. An empty string is the only value that makes both sides agree,
because `'' ?? x` short-circuits to '' where a missing key would not.
packageName is otherwise only used for samples/package.json, which does not
exist here, and the changelog heading. The version write into
apps/desktop/package.json is keyed on path, so it is unaffected.
